summary: TechCrunch reports that OpenAI's board fired CEO Sam Altman on November 17, 2023, saying he "wasn't consistently candid in his communications" and that it no longer had confidence in his ability to lead. CTO Mira Murati became interim CEO and Greg Brockman stepped down as board chairman but stays as president. The article covers reactions, the board's makeup, OpenAI's nonprofit-controlled structure, and Microsoft's response as its major investor.
one_line: OpenAI's board fired CEO Sam Altman for not being consistently candid, naming CTO Mira Murati interim CEO while Microsoft reaffirmed its partnership.
key_facts: Sam Altman was fired from OpenAI, Inc., the 501(c)(3) nonprofit that governs OpenAI, and leaves both the board and the CEO role.

OpenAI's blog said a "deliberative review process by the board" concluded Altman "wasn't consistently candid in his communications" with the board, hindering its ability to exercise its responsibilities.
Mira Murati, previously OpenAI's CTO, was appointed interim CEO, and OpenAI said it will immediately begin a formal search for a permanent CEO.
Greg Brockman, a co-founder, steps down as board chairman but remains OpenAI's president, reporting to Murati.
The remaining board consists of Ilya Sutskever, Adam D'Angelo, Tasha McCauley and Helen Toner.
The firing was unexpected: OpenAI had hosted its first developer conference, OpenAI DevDay, the prior week, which Altman emceed, and employees reportedly learned of it when it was announced publicly.
Altman co-founded OpenAI with Peter Thiel, Reid Hoffman and others, and was initially co-chair alongside Elon Musk, who left in 2018 to avoid a conflict of interest with Tesla.
Over recent months Altman appeared at U.S. congressional hearings and met world leaders including Joe Biden, Olaf Scholz and Emmanuel Macron on an international policy tour.
OpenAI Global, LLC, the for-profit subsidiary, is fully controlled by the nonprofit, whose board can determine when AGI is achieved and exclude it from IP licenses, including with Microsoft.
Microsoft has invested $13 billion in OpenAI, holds what amounts to a 49% stake, and its stock fell more than 1% in the last 30 minutes of trading after the news.
Axios reported Microsoft was notified "minutes" before the public announcement.
OpenAI was founded as a nonprofit in 2015 and restructured in 2019 as a "capped-profit" company to raise capital.
Altman told the Financial Times that week he "hoped" Microsoft would increase its investment to cover huge model training costs.
Microsoft's Frank Shaw and Satya Nadella said Microsoft remains committed to its long-term partnership with OpenAI, and to Mira and the team.
